test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (JSO) 2022 Official Paper (Held On: 4 March 2023)
subject: general
question: Suppose a number is chosen at random from the set {1,2,3,4}. For events A: {1,3}. B: {1,2} and C: {1,4}, which of the following does NOT hold?

options.text: A, B and C are independent

solution:
The correct answer is **A, B and C are independent **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** In probability, two events A and B are said to be independent if the occurrence of one does not affect the probability of the occurrence of the other.

In other words, if A and B are independent, then P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B).

If three events A, B, and C are independent, then the following must hold: 

 
• P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B)
 
• P(A ∩ C) = P(A) × P(C)
 
• P(B ∩ C) = P(B) × P(C)
 
• P(A ∩ B ∩ C) = P(A) × P(B) × P(C)

Given the events are A: {1,3}, B: {1,2}, and C: {1,4}
The probability of occurrence of events A, B and C are P(A) = P(B) = P(C) = 0.5 as there are two favourable outcomes out of four. 

The probabilities of intersections are: 

 
• P(A ∩ B) = 1/4 = 0.25 
 
• P(A ∩ C) = 1/4 = 0.25
 
• P(B ∩ C) = 1/4 = 0.25
 
• P(A ∩ B ∩ C) = 1/4 = 0.25

​Conditions for independence are as follows: 

 
• P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B): 0.25 = 0.5 × 0.5 - True
 
• P(A ∩ C) = P(A) × P(C): 0.25 = 0.5 × 0.5 - True
 
• P(B ∩ C) = P(B) × P(C): 0.25 = 0.5 × 0.5 - True
 
• P(A ∩ B ∩ C) = P(A) × P(B) × P(C): 0.25 ≠ 0.5 × 0.5 × 0.5 - False

**​Hence, when selecting from the set {1,2,3,4}, the events A: {1,3}, B: {1,2}, and C: {1,4} are not mutually independent, despite their pairwise independence.**
